3. Ex-(≈0.814) → “Ex- prefix”: Detects the “Ex-” prefix in news headlines to signal a person’s former role or title (ex-minister, ex-FBI boss, ex-wrestler).  
4. –(0.774) → “Element-list hyphen”: Highlights hyphens linking chemical element symbols in multi-metal formulas or compositional lists (Fe-Ni, Co-Cu, etc.).  
5. Inter-(≈0.773) → “Inter- prefix”: Picks up words beginning with “Inter-” in scientific/medical contexts (inter-comparison, inter-observer, inter-ictal) indicating between-entity relationships or processes.  
6. trying(0.769) → “trying (gerund)”: Fires on the present-participle “trying” in first-person anecdotal narratives describing personal attempts or experiences.  
7. Pre-(≈0.750) → “Pre- prefix”: Highlights “Pre-” prefixes in cooking, physiology, policy or medical definitions (preheat, pre/postjunctional, pre-existing, pre-diabetes) marking “before” states or actions.  
8. impossible(0.749) → “impossible”: Flags the strong negative adjective “impossible,” denoting categorical infeasibility or absolute denial in technical discussion.  
9. determines(0.740) → “determines”: Captures the verb “determines” in research contexts, signaling sentences that specify factors or mechanisms that decide outcomes.  
10. decide(0.739) → “decide”: Activates on the verb “decide” in informal/advice writing, marking choice-making or decision-guidance language.

• HG  
  Recognizes the UK postcode prefix “HG” (and its numbered districts HG1–HG5) referring to Harrogate-area mail zones.

  Captures the acronym LGBT in discussions of the LGBT community, rights, harassment and legal protections.  

• GLW  
  Detects the “GLW” abbreviation in corporate/legal contexts (e.g. GLW Broadband, Inc.).  

• Social  
  Marks the word “Social” when it heads programs or initiatives—most notably Social Security or branded social-maturity/index concepts.  

• SF  
  Identifies the “SF” prefix in product or brand names (e.g. limited-edition SF X t-shirts).  

• LDL  
  Triggers on “LDL” in biomedical settings referring to low-density lipoprotein and its receptor.  

• MHC  
  Captures “MHC” in immunology texts denoting major histocompatibility complex class II antigens.  

• GLUT  
  Recognizes the “GLUT” prefix in glucose-transporter gene/protein names (e.g. GLUT1, GLUT4) in cell-biology papers.

direction_summaries.explanation:
Here’s a concise concept label for each highlighted-token feature based on its top activations and contexts:

1. Determ(1.000) → “Determination”: Marks the “Determination of …” construction in scientific titles, flagging papers that report analytical measurement methods.  
2. Direct(0.819) → “Direct …”: Captures the adjective “Direct” at the start of scientific‐method titles, denoting protocols or assays performed without intermediates.  
3. Ex-(≈0.814) → “Ex- prefix”: Detects the “Ex-” prefix in news headlines to signal a person’s former role or title (ex-minister, ex-FBI boss, ex-wrestler).  
4. –(0.774) → “Element-list hyphen”: Highlights hyphens linking chemical element symbols in multi-metal formulas or compositional lists (Fe-Ni, Co-Cu, etc.).  
5. Inter-(≈0.773) → “Inter- prefix”: Picks up words beginning with “Inter-” in scientific/medical contexts (inter-comparison, inter-observer, inter-ictal) indicating between-entity relationships or processes.  
6. trying(0.769) → “trying (gerund)”: Fires on the present-participle “trying” in first-person anecdotal narratives describing personal attempts or experiences.  
7. Pre-(≈0.750) → “Pre- prefix”: Highlights “Pre-” prefixes in cooking, physiology, policy or medical definitions (preheat, pre/postjunctional, pre-existing, pre-diabetes) marking “before” states or actions.  
8. impossible(0.749) → “impossible”: Flags the strong negative adjective “impossible,” denoting categorical infeasibility or absolute denial in technical discussion.  
9. determines(0.740) → “determines”: Captures the verb “determines” in research contexts, signaling sentences that specify factors or mechanisms that decide outcomes.  
10. decide(0.739) → “decide”: Activates on the verb “decide” in informal/advice writing, marking choice-making or decision-guidance language.
